text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows two applications to communicate by exchanging data, usually through HTTP requests such as GET or POST. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access an API, you often need authentication, for example an API key, to prove your identity. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can send in a certain time. Finally, good error handling helps you manage failed requests and unexpected responses gracefully.
